intro: Hobbies at home and outside, games, and the queue at the cinema.
p.afición.consejo: The plural «aficiones» loses the accent. «Ser aficionado a» something means you like it a lot.
p.jardinería.consejo: It comes from «jardín». The person who does it is «el jardinero».
p.bricolaje.consejo: It comes from French. The j sounds h: bri-ko-LA-he. You say «hacer bricolaje».
p.crucigrama.consejo: It is masculine: «el crucigrama». The verb is «hacer un crucigrama».
p.coleccionar.consejo: It comes from «colección»: «colecciono sellos». It is written with two c's.
p.sello.consejo: It is stuck on letters. It is also the ink mark stamped on a paper.
p.moneda.consejo: It is also a country's own money: «la moneda» of that country.
p.juego de mesa.consejo: With «jugar» you use «a»: «jugar a un juego de mesa».
p.dardos.consejo: It is almost always plural: «jugar a los dardos». The target is the «diana».
p.billar.consejo: The double l sounds «y»: bi-YAR. You say «jugar al billar».
p.raqueta.consejo: It is used in tennis and badminton. In Spanish it is written «raqueta», not «racket».
p.chándal.consejo: It has an accent on the «á»: CHAN-dal. You wear it to run, exercise or just be comfortable.
p.fila.consejo: At the cinema: «la primera fila». If people wait for their turn, it is a «cola».
p.cola.consejo: You say «hacer cola». It is also the back part of an animal's body.
b1.texto:
Today we talk about hobbies, games and shows.

- **Hobbies:** **jardinería**, **bricolaje**, **crucigramas**. You can **coleccionar** **sellos** or **monedas**. If you like something a lot, you are «aficionado» to it.
- **Going out:** having a picnic, going camping, sightseeing, going for tapas.
- **Games:** a **juego de mesa** has a board, counters and a die. In a bar there are **dardos** and **billar**. With them you use **jugar a**.
- **Sport:** a tennis **raqueta**, a football. The **chándal** is the clothing for sport.
- **Shows:** at the box office you queue (**hacer cola**); on the ticket it says the **fila** and the seat. The spectators are the audience.
- **On TV:** a series has episodes; for children there are cartoons.
b2.f1.texto: We can play darts or pool.
b2.f2.texto: I'd rather finish the crossword in the paper.
b2.f3.texto: Then I'll sort my stamp collection.
b2.f4.texto: Do you still collect old coins?
b2.f5.texto: I have more than a hundred coins.
b2.f6.texto: Better we go to the cinema after lunch.
b2.f7.texto: Then we leave early so as not to queue.
b2.f8.texto: In the front row my neck hurts.
b4.texto:
With **jugar** you use **a** and the name of the game or sport:

- **jugar a** los dardos · **jugar a** un juego de mesa
- **jugar al** billar (**a + el = al**)

The verb **jugar** changes the **u** into **ue**: juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan.

For other hobbies you use **hacer**: **hacer** crucigramas, **hacer** bricolaje, **hacer** jardinería. And with **coleccionar** no preposition is needed: **coleccionar** sellos.
b4.e0.texto: My cousins play pool on Saturdays.
b4.e2.texto: My grandfather does crosswords in the garden.
b5.f0.texto: In Bruno's attic, a yellow light falls on a table with many boxes.
b5.f1.texto: Inside each box sleep stamps from faraway countries.
b5.f2.texto: Bruno touches them with tweezers and looks at them in the light.
b5.f3.texto: Some old coins shine like little suns.
b5.f4.texto: Each one keeps the story of a journey.
b5.f5.texto: In the afternoon, Clara puts on her tracksuit and picks up her racket.
b5.f6.texto: In the park, the air smells of recent rain.
b5.f7.texto: A girl hits the ball with her red racket.
b5.f8.texto: Her brother watches her from the front row of benches.
b5.f9.texto: In the end the two of them queue at the kiosk to buy an ice cream.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! Gardening is looking after plants and flowers.
b6.o1.refuerzo: DIY is fixing things at home with your hands.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A crossword is a word game, not a plant hobby.
b6.pregunta: Which hobby is done in the garden?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Jugar» needs «a» before the game: «a los dardos».
b7.o1.refuerzo: That's it! You say «jugar a los dardos».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Con» does not work here: games take «a».
b8.frase: Mis primos juegan al billar los sábados
b8.traduccion: My cousins play pool on Saturdays
b9.o0.refuerzo: A racket is not clothing: it is a tennis object.
b9.o1.refuerzo: A stamp goes on a letter; it is not clothing.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! The tracksuit is comfortable clothing for sport.
b9.pregunta: What clothes do you put on to run?
b11.o0.refuerzo: That's it! Crosswords are done with «hacer».
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Jugar» goes with «a» and a game; with crosswords you use «hacer».
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Poner» is not used with crosswords. The natural verb is «hacer».
b12.o0.refuerzo: DIY is fixing or making things with your hands.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That's it! To «coleccionar» is to gather objects of the same kind.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Bowling is a game, not gathering objects.
b12.pregunta: You gather old coins from many countries. What do you do?
p.ordeno.consejo: From «ordenar»: «ordeno» means I put in order.
p.colección.consejo: «Colección» is a set of collected objects.
p.coleccionas.consejo: From «coleccionar»: the verb is about gathering objects.
p.antiguas.consejo: «Antiguo» means old; the feminine plural is «antiguas».
p.cuello.consejo: «Cuello» is the neck; the ll-like y sounds as in English «yes».
p.crucigramas.consejo: «Crucigrama» is a crossword puzzle; the plural adds «-s».
p.pinzas.consejo: «Pinza» is a pair of tweezers or a peg.
p.algunas.consejo: «Algunas» is the feminine plural of «alguno»: some.
p.soles.consejo: Plural of «sol»; in a sentence it can mean a sunny sparkle.
p.coge.consejo: From «coger»: in Spain it means to take or pick up.
p.bancos.consejo: «Banco» is a bench; it can also mean a bank.
